education.degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

experience.title: Middleware Engineer
bullets: Led 4 customer Statements of Work, partnering directly with customers to scope requirements, break work into engineering deliverables, and coordinate execution across frontend, database, and middleware teams.

For 2 of those engagements, independently designed and built the complete solution—from database changes and REST APIs to business logic, frontend functionality, and customer-specific configuration—through production deployment.
Shipped 120+ full-stack production tickets (PHP/PostgreSQL backend, JavaScript/Handlebars frontend), owning application-layer business logic for customer-facing enterprise workflows.

Refactored legacy AJAX frontend into internal REST APIs to centralize business rules; worked directly with customers and product architects to translate requirements into shipped features and resolve reported production issues.

experience.title: Technical Co-founder
bullets: Founded Northhealth AI, a clinician-first rehab platform that turns continuous patient data into provider insight at visits and personalized recovery support between visits.
Led engineering and shipped the platform to its v1 release, the version the company used to begin clinical trials.

Accepted to present at the American Academy of Neurology (AAN) in 2026; validated direction with 22 healthcare organizations and professionals, incorporating clinician feedback into MVP scope, safety constraints, and workflow design.

experience.title: Undergraduate Researcher
bullets: Developed and refined machine learning models in PyTorch for real-time cybersecurity threat detection in simulated nuclear systems, improving anomaly detection accuracy and real-time responsiveness under operational constraints.
Built a reproducible, containerized simulation environment using Docker and ICSSIM to support high-fidelity nuclear flow loop testing for model training and evaluation.

experience.title: Software Engineer Intern
bullets: Engineered a Java-based automation platform integrating 9 heterogeneous systems (databases, internal tools, web interfaces), reducing workflow time by 70% and significantly improving reliability.
Designed a unified data model and adapter layer to normalize inconsistent schema, handle legacy edge cases, and enable deterministic cross-system synchronization.

projects.title: AlphaResearch
projects.org: UC Berkeley AI Hackathon — Best Use of Cognition
bullets: Built a cloud-orchestrated recursive **multi-agent** research platform where agents recursively spawn specialized sub-agents for parallel hypothesis generation, experimentation, and distributed computation, enabling scalable research across 1000+ agents.

Built the distributed runtime: a **Google Cloud Run** orchestrator, isolated **Modal** sandboxes per agent with a shared compute budget, **Redis** state and event bus, **GCS** artifact storage, **FastAPI** + SSE API, and a **Next.js** live agent-tree dashboard.
Tested the distributed runtime for parallel CPU-only experimentation, reaching 500,000+ MiniGrid training steps/sec across concurrent sandboxes under a shared budget.

projects.title: Personal Telemetry Platform
bullets: Building a personal telemetry platform that ingests continuous multimodal streams — **Omi** and **Garmin** wearables for continuous audio and biometrics, plus passive desktop and ambient activity — through self-written capture and ingestion code into one time-aligned longitudinal store.

Shipped the platform's control plane end to end: a **Python** CLI, **FastAPI** services as the single database client, hosted **Supabase/Postgres** behind a private schema with **Google OAuth**, and deterministic ingestion pipelines that normalize and persist hundreds of records per run.

Designing the modeling layer above capture: time-aligning heterogeneous streams, **feature engineering** over raw audio and biometric signals, and correlating environment and activity against physiological response to build a personal **time-series** model of state and focus.

projects.title: Tiny Object Tracking
bullets: Extended **MKDNet** in **PyTorch** on a large-scale tiny-object tracking dataset, then adapted it to a novel small-object domain for up to 39% accuracy increase over the base MKDNet model.

Reproduced the published baseline before adapting it, then evaluated the adapted model against that baseline under a matched **evaluation protocol**, establishing the 39% gain as a controlled comparison rather than a single run.
